authority_note.documentation_rule: Human-readable pin statements elsewhere (integrations/*/README.md, docs/engine_setup.md) must cite this file and must not restate commits. On any disagreement, this file wins.
authority_note.dual_identity: Forge carries two distinct identities that must never be conflated. secondary_engine.commit is the Rules-Core authority (the engine identity the bridge reports and Rules qualification binds to). secondary_engine.bridge_source is the materialization source actually cloned and built (repository, exact commit, and the Rules-Core base commit it must descend from). The bridge source contains the Rules Core plus additive bridge surfaces; it is not a new Rules-Core version.

engine_identity_pb09.confusion_forbidden: FIVE Forge commits are distinct here: the pinned upstream core, the Lab fork, the materializing bridge, the fork-side bridge/evidence head, and the WSR20 native-suite descendant. Ancestry is not identity, a descendant is a different tree, and a bridge commit is not an engine commit. None of these fields licenses reporting a result observed on one as evidence for another.

truth_boundary: B4-D is external_rules_engine evidence for real pinned XMage deck import, Commander construction/start, live state observation, current-priority decision/legal-action handoff, real priority passing, stale decision/action rejection, bounded submission-ready targetless/nonmodal action execution including a real Rograkh commander cast, an externally exportable monotonic bridge audit event stream with action/decision identity and pre/post state hashes, and explicit per-game XMage lifecycle cleanup/reuse. The audit stream covers real bridge/XMage lifecycle and externally controlled action boundaries; it is not claimed to be an exhaustive raw internal XMage GameEvent tap. Globally complete legal-action enumeration and action submission remain unproven because target, mode, choice and combat classes are incomplete. Mulligan, seed-control, replay and complete production game-loop coverage remain unproven. This is not win-rate evidence and does not make XMage a production-ready provider.
